```{r create_kaplan_meier_plots}
# ==============================
# Create Kaplan-Meier Survival Curves
# ==============================

# Function to create Kaplan-Meier plot with detailed diagnostics
create_km_plot <- function(data, time_var, event_var, group_var, title) {
  # Initial data check
  if (is.null(data) || nrow(data) == 0) {
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  # Clean data
  data_clean <- data %>%
    filter(!is.na(.data[[time_var]]), !is.na(.data[[event_var]]), 
           .data[[time_var]] > 0, !is.na(.data[[group_var]]),
           !str_detect(tolower(.data[[group_var]]), "no ctdna data"))
  
  if (nrow(data_clean) == 0) {
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  # Check events
  n_events <- sum(data_clean[[event_var]] == 1, na.rm = TRUE)
  if (n_events == 0) {
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  # Check groups - get unique groups
  unique_groups <- unique(data_clean[[group_var]])
  unique_groups <- unique_groups[!is.na(unique_groups)]
  
  if (length(unique_groups) < 2) {
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  # Ensure group variable is a factor for proper plotting
  data_clean[[group_var]] <- as.factor(data_clean[[group_var]])
  
  # Create survival formula
  surv_formula <- as.formula(paste0("Surv(", time_var, ", ", event_var, ") ~ ", group_var))
  
  # Fit survival model
  surv_fit <- tryCatch({
    fit <- survfit(surv_formula, data = data_clean)
    if (is.null(fit) || length(fit$strata) == 0) {
      return(NULL)
    }
    fit
  }, error = function(e) {
    return(NULL)
  })
  
  if (is.null(surv_fit)) {
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  # Create plot
  p <- tryCatch({
    ggsurvplot(
      surv_fit,
      data = data_clean,
      pval = TRUE,
      pval.method = TRUE,
      conf.int = FALSE,
      risk.table = TRUE,
      risk.table.height = 0.25,
      ggtheme = theme_minimal(),
      title = title,
      xlab = "Time from 6-Month Landmark (months)",
      ylab = "Overall Survival Probability",
      legend.title = "Group",
      palette = "Set1",
      fontsize = 3.5
    )
  }, error = function(e) {
    # Try simpler plot if full plot fails
    tryCatch({
      ggsurvplot(
        surv_fit,
        data = data_clean,
        pval = TRUE,
        conf.int = FALSE,
        risk.table = TRUE,
        ggtheme = theme_minimal(),
        title = title,
        xlab = "Time from 6-Month Landmark (months)",
        ylab = "Overall Survival Probability",
        legend.title = "Group",
        palette = "Set1"
      )
    }, error = function(e2) {
      return(NULL)
    })
  })
  
  return(p)
}
```

```{r additional_analyses, include=FALSE}
# ==============================
# Additional Analyses for Model Comparison
# ==============================

# 1. Hazard Ratios and Effect Sizes
calculate_hr_table <- function(data, time_var, event_var, group_var) {
  data_clean <- data %>%
    filter(!is.na(.data[[time_var]]), !is.na(.data[[event_var]]), 
           .data[[time_var]] > 0, !is.na(.data[[group_var]]),
           !str_detect(tolower(.data[[group_var]]), "no ctdna data"))
  
  if (nrow(data_clean) == 0 || sum(data_clean[[event_var]] == 1, na.rm = TRUE) == 0) {
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  # Get reference group (usually the group with best prognosis)
  unique_groups <- unique(data_clean[[group_var]])
  unique_groups <- unique_groups[!is.na(unique_groups)]
  
  if (length(unique_groups) < 2) {
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  # Use different reference groups for qualitative vs quantitative
  # Qualitative: Persistent Negative
  # Quantitative: Persistent Negative
  if (group_var == "qualitative_group") {
    if ("Persistent Negative" %in% unique(data_clean[[group_var]])) {
      reference_group <- "Persistent Negative"
      # Set Persistent Negative as reference level
      data_clean[[group_var]] <- relevel(as.factor(data_clean[[group_var]]), ref = "Persistent Negative")
    } else {
      # Fallback: group with best prognosis
      group_stats <- data_clean %>%
        group_by(.data[[group_var]]) %>%
        summarise(
          n = n(),
          events = sum(.data[[event_var]] == 1, na.rm = TRUE),
          event_rate = events / n,
          .groups = "drop"
        ) %>%
        mutate(adequate_size = n >= 5) %>%
        arrange(adequate_size, event_rate, desc(n))
      
      reference_group <- as.character(group_stats[[group_var]][1])
    }
  } else if (group_var == "quantitative_group") {
    # For quantitative, use Persistent Negative as reference
    if ("Persistent Negative" %in% unique(data_clean[[group_var]])) {
      reference_group <- "Persistent Negative"
      # Set Persistent Negative as reference level
      data_clean[[group_var]] <- relevel(as.factor(data_clean[[group_var]]), ref = "Persistent Negative")
    } else {
      # Fallback: group with best prognosis
      group_stats <- data_clean %>%
        group_by(.data[[group_var]]) %>%
        summarise(
          n = n(),
          events = sum(.data[[event_var]] == 1, na.rm = TRUE),
          event_rate = events / n,
          .groups = "drop"
        ) %>%
        mutate(adequate_size = n >= 5) %>%
        arrange(adequate_size, event_rate, desc(n))
      
      reference_group <- as.character(group_stats[[group_var]][1])
    }
  } else {
    # Fallback: group with best prognosis - lowest event rate, but with adequate sample size
    group_stats <- data_clean %>%
      group_by(.data[[group_var]]) %>%
      summarise(
        n = n(),
        events = sum(.data[[event_var]] == 1, na.rm = TRUE),
        event_rate = events / n,
        .groups = "drop"
      ) %>%
      # Prefer groups with at least 5 patients for reference
      mutate(adequate_size = n >= 5) %>%
      arrange(adequate_size, event_rate, desc(n))
    
    reference_group <- as.character(group_stats[[group_var]][1])
    # Set reference level
    data_clean[[group_var]] <- relevel(as.factor(data_clean[[group_var]]), ref = reference_group)
  }
  
  # Fit Cox model with reference level set
  surv_formula <- as.formula(paste0("Surv(", time_var, ", ", event_var, ") ~ ", group_var))
  cox_fit <- tryCatch({
    coxph(surv_formula, data = data_clean)
  }, error = function(e) {
    return(NULL)
  })
  
  if (is.null(cox_fit)) {
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  # Extract HRs
  cox_summary <- summary(cox_fit)
  hr_df <- as.data.frame(cox_summary$conf.int)
  hr_df$Group <- rownames(hr_df)
  rownames(hr_df) <- NULL
  
  hr_table <- hr_df %>%
    mutate(
      Group = str_remove(Group, paste0(group_var, "=")),
      HR = `exp(coef)`,
      HR_Lower = `lower .95`,
      HR_Upper = `upper .95`,
      P_Value = cox_summary$coefficients[, "Pr(>|z|)"]
    ) %>%
    # Remove reference group from table (it's HR = 1.0 by definition)
    filter(Group != reference_group) %>%
    # Clean any remaining variable name prefixes
    mutate(Group = str_remove(Group, paste0("^", group_var, ""))) %>%
    select(Group, HR, HR_Lower, HR_Upper, P_Value)
  
  return(list(hr_table = hr_table, reference_group = reference_group))
}

# Calculate HRs for each approach
hr_qualitative_result <- calculate_hr_table(survival_qualitative, "os_time_landmark", "death_event_landmark", "qualitative_group")
hr_qualitative <- if (!is.null(hr_qualitative_result)) hr_qualitative_result$hr_table else NULL
ref_qualitative <- if (!is.null(hr_qualitative_result)) hr_qualitative_result$reference_group else NULL

hr_quantitative_result <- calculate_hr_table(survival_quantitative, "os_time_landmark", "death_event_landmark", "quantitative_group")
hr_quantitative <- if (!is.null(hr_quantitative_result)) hr_quantitative_result$hr_table else NULL
ref_quantitative <- if (!is.null(hr_quantitative_result)) hr_quantitative_result$reference_group else NULL

# Note: Quantitative approach now uses ctDNA-RECIST criteria (see definitions above)

# 2. Missing Data Analysis
missing_data_analysis <- survival_outcomes_landmark %>%
  left_join(qualitative_groups %>% select(patient_id, qualitative_group), by = "patient_id") %>%
  left_join(quantitative_groups %>% select(patient_id, quantitative_group), by = "patient_id") %>%
  mutate(
    has_qualitative = !is.na(qualitative_group) & !str_detect(tolower(qualitative_group), "no ctdna data"),
    has_quantitative = !is.na(quantitative_group) & !str_detect(tolower(quantitative_group), "no ctdna data"),
    has_both = has_qualitative & has_quantitative,
    has_qual_only = has_qualitative & !has_quantitative,
    has_quant_only = has_quantitative & !has_qualitative,
    has_neither = !has_qualitative & !has_quantitative
  )

missing_summary <- tibble(
  Category = c("Both models", "Qualitative only", "Quantitative only", "Neither model", "Total"),
  N = c(
    sum(missing_data_analysis$has_both, na.rm = TRUE),
    sum(missing_data_analysis$has_qual_only, na.rm = TRUE),
    sum(missing_data_analysis$has_quant_only, na.rm = TRUE),
    sum(missing_data_analysis$has_neither, na.rm = TRUE),
    nrow(missing_data_analysis)
  )
)

# 3. Group Distribution Comparison
group_dist_qual <- survival_qualitative %>%
  filter(!is.na(qualitative_group), !str_detect(tolower(qualitative_group), "no ctdna data"),
         !is.na(os_time_landmark), !is.na(death_event_landmark), os_time_landmark > 0) %>%
  count(qualitative_group, death_event_landmark) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = death_event_landmark, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) %>%
  mutate(
    Total = `0` + `1`,
    Event_Rate = round(`1` / Total * 100, 1)
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(Event_Rate))

group_dist_quant <- survival_quantitative %>%
  filter(!is.na(quantitative_group), !str_detect(tolower(quantitative_group), "no ctdna data"),
         !is.na(os_time_landmark), !is.na(death_event_landmark), os_time_landmark > 0) %>%
  count(quantitative_group, death_event_landmark) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = death_event_landmark, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) %>%
  mutate(
    Total = `0` + `1`,
    Event_Rate = round(`1` / Total * 100, 1)
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(Event_Rate))

# 4. Median Survival Times
calculate_median_survival <- function(data, time_var, event_var, group_var) {
  data_clean <- data %>%
    filter(!is.na(.data[[time_var]]), !is.na(.data[[event_var]]), 
           .data[[time_var]] > 0, !is.na(.data[[group_var]]),
           !str_detect(tolower(.data[[group_var]]), "no ctdna data"))
  
  if (nrow(data_clean) == 0) {
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  surv_formula <- as.formula(paste0("Surv(", time_var, ", ", event_var, ") ~ ", group_var))
  surv_fit <- tryCatch({
    survfit(surv_formula, data = data_clean)
  }, error = function(e) {
    return(NULL)
  })
  
  if (is.null(surv_fit)) {
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  # Extract median survival
  median_surv <- summary(surv_fit)$table[, "median"]
  median_surv_df <- data.frame(
    Group = names(median_surv),
    Median_Survival_Months = round(median_surv, 1)
  ) %>%
    mutate(Group = str_remove(Group, paste0(group_var, "=")))
  
  return(median_surv_df)
}
```

```{r conclusions_and_limitations, echo=FALSE}
cat("\n## Conclusions\n\n")

cat("### Main Findings\n\n")

cat("This analysis compared three approaches for classifying ctDNA response patterns and their association with overall survival in patients with bladder cancer:\n\n")

cat("1. **Qualitative Approach**: Binary classification based on ctDNA status changes\n")
cat("2. **Quantitative Approach**: Classification based on percent change from most recent ctDNA assessment\n")
cat("3. **Machine Learning Approach**: Unsupervised clustering using multiple ctDNA kinetic features\n\n")

cat("**Key Conclusions:**\n\n")

cat("- All three approaches demonstrated good to excellent discriminatory performance for overall survival, with C-indices generally above 0.80 across most patient subgroups.\n\n")

cat("- Model performance varied by therapy setting: The 'No Systemic Therapy' group (representing earlier-stage disease) consistently showed the highest C-index values (>0.95) across all three models, suggesting that ctDNA-based classification may be particularly valuable for risk stratification in earlier-stage disease.\n\n")

cat("- The Quantitative approach showed variable performance across therapy types, with notably lower C-index in the Palliative setting (0.709) compared to other therapy types, while maintaining strong performance in other settings.\n\n")

cat("- Pairwise comparisons between models (shown in Table 2) tested for significant differences in C-index values. The results indicate whether one approach demonstrates superior discriminatory performance compared to others.\n\n")

cat("- Sensitivity analyses by histology type (Urothelial Carcinoma of Bladder vs UTUC or Variant Histology) and therapy type (Neoadjuvant, Adjuvant, Palliative, No Systemic Therapy) demonstrated that model performance is generally consistent across these subgroups, though some differences were observed.\n\n")

cat("### Clinical Implications\n\n")

cat("These findings suggest that ctDNA response classification can effectively stratify patients by survival risk. The choice of classification approach may depend on the clinical setting and patient population. The superior performance observed in earlier-stage disease (No Systemic Therapy group) highlights the potential value of ctDNA monitoring for risk stratification when treatment decisions are more nuanced.\n\n")

cat("## Limitations\n\n")

cat("Several limitations should be considered when interpreting these results:\n\n")

cat("1. **Retrospective Analysis**: This is a retrospective analysis of existing data, which may be subject to selection bias and confounding factors not accounted for in the analysis.\n\n")

cat("2. **Landmark Analysis**: The 6-month landmark analysis, while reducing immortal time bias, excludes patients who died within 6 months of their baseline ctDNA measurement. This may limit generalizability to patients with very poor prognosis.\n\n")

cat("3. **Sample Size**: Some subgroups (particularly in therapy-specific analyses) had relatively small sample sizes, which may limit the precision of C-index estimates and the power to detect significant differences between models.\n\n")

cat("4. **Patient Overlap Across Therapy Groups**: Patients could be counted in multiple therapy categories if they received multiple types of therapy during their ctDNA monitoring period. While this reflects clinical reality, it may complicate interpretation of therapy-specific analyses.\n\n")

cat("5. **Missing Data**: Patients without valid ctDNA classifications for all three approaches were excluded from the comparative analysis, potentially introducing selection bias.\n\n")

cat("6. **Temporal Relationships**: The analysis does not account for the temporal relationship between ctDNA measurements and therapy administration, which may influence ctDNA dynamics.\n\n")

cat("7. **External Validation**: These models have not been validated in an independent external cohort, limiting generalizability to other patient populations.\n\n")

cat("8. **Treatment Heterogeneity**: The analysis includes patients with diverse treatment regimens, which may introduce heterogeneity that affects model performance.\n\n")

cat("## Next Steps\n\n")

cat("Based on these findings, the following next steps are recommended:\n\n")

cat("1. **Prospective Validation**: The best-performing model(s) should be prospectively validated in an independent cohort to confirm generalizability and clinical utility.\n\n")

cat("2. **Refinement of Classification Criteria**: Consider refining classification thresholds, particularly for the Quantitative approach, to optimize performance across different therapy settings.\n\n")

cat("3. **Integration with Clinical Factors**: Future analyses should explore whether combining ctDNA classification with clinical factors (stage, histology, treatment history) improves predictive performance.\n\n")

cat("4. **Time-Dependent Analysis**: Consider time-dependent analyses that account for the temporal relationship between ctDNA changes and outcomes, potentially using landmark analyses at multiple timepoints.\n\n")

cat("5. **Therapy-Specific Models**: Given the observed variation in model performance across therapy types, consider developing therapy-specific classification approaches or thresholds.\n\n")

cat("6. **Larger Sample Sizes**: Expand the analysis to include larger sample sizes, particularly for therapy-specific and histology-specific subgroups, to improve precision and power.\n\n")

cat("7. **External Validation Cohort**: Validate findings in an independent external cohort with different patient characteristics and treatment patterns.\n\n")

cat("8. **Clinical Decision Support**: Develop clinical decision support tools that incorporate the best-performing ctDNA classification approach to guide treatment decisions in real-world settings.\n\n")

cat("9. **Cost-Effectiveness Analysis**: Evaluate the cost-effectiveness of implementing ctDNA-based classification approaches compared to standard clinical assessment methods.\n\n")

cat("10. **Longitudinal Monitoring**: Explore optimal timing and frequency of ctDNA assessments for risk stratification and treatment monitoring.\n\n")
```
